Citigroup finalized a settlement for Euro-denominated sovereign debt price-fixing with court approval in December 2024. Both disclosures involve major banks as defendants in antitrust suits alleging manipulation of financial benchmarks.

sentences.text: In February 2021, purchasers of Euro-denominated sovereign debt issued by European central governments added CGMI, CGML, and others as defendants to a putative class action, captioned IN RE EUROPEAN GOVERNMENT BONDS ANTITRUST LITIGATION, in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York.
On December 9, 2024, the court granted final approval of plaintiffs' settlement of the action with certain defendants, including CGMI and CGML.

Group Inc., GS&Co. and GSI were among the defendants named in a putative antitrust class action relating to the settlement of credit default swaps, filed on June 30, 2021 in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Mexico.

On January 24, 2024, the court granted the defendants' motion to stay the proceedings pending the resolution of the motion filed by the defendants on November 3, 2023 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York to enforce a 2015 settlement and release among the parties.

comparisons.peer_topic: Settlement of Gilt Price Fixing Litigation
comparisons.peer_summary: On September 16, 2024, a court dismissed without prejudice a class action complaint alleging price-fixing of gilts traded in the U.S. between 2009 and 2013; subsequently, the Firm and other defendants reached an agreement in principle to settle the U.S. litigation.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Morgan Stanley disclose the resolution of antitrust litigation involving government bond pricing and settlements in 2024. Citigroup’s disclosure details the final court approval of a settlement for Euro-denominated sovereign debt price-fixing claims in December 2024. Similarly, Morgan Stanley discloses reaching an agreement in principle to settle U.S. litigation regarding gilt price-fixing claims in late 2024, following a dismissal without prejudice in September 2024. Both represent the conclusion of specific government bond antitrust conspiracies through settlement mechanisms.

sentences.text: On December 9, 2024, the court granted final approval of plaintiffs' settlement of the action with certain defendants, including CGMI and CGML.
